items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: One of my great friends that lives in New York, Rockmore, he's part-Indian.

ctx.x: Well, he'd line up one town after another. I guess he had some kind of map. He would line up one town... The jumps wasn't over 25 or 100 miles. We didn't have no long jumps. But I remember, we went all the way out to some place in Utah... I know we went... I saw the Grand Canyon early in my life. We just drove by it, and you looked... We just drove on a road where you could look over and look down and see it. And then the colors were so beautiful. And I met those Indians... The prettiest women out there was those…

One of my great friends that lives in New York, Rockmore, he's part-Indian. I don't know whether Rockmore... I think Rockmore had a little land... Because we had a couple of kids in the school that come from them (?) people, you know, that had a little money. Because if you was an Indian or part-Indian, and if you were just born in Oklahoma, you got land. And I always think, boy, what would have happened to me if I had been born a month and ten days... I always say I was born a month and ten days late, because…
